# Results — Study 856 (Book-Tax Differences)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a **large
positive book-minus-tax income difference** (book pretax income far above the taxable income
implied by the tax expense) marks **less persistent earnings** and predicts **lower future
returns** (Hanlon 2005). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `d579ef33a57f` (yfinance daily adjusted closes); events
cache = 569 (ticker, fiscal-year) rows.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **39** of a 42-name large-cap US filer basket (fixed, current survivors); 3 names (ABT, KO, MCD) lacked a clean long-history pretax-income XBRL tag and dropped out |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: annual (10-K) `IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxes...` (pretax), `IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit` (tax), `Assets`; longest per-name history, de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **569** fiscal-year events, period ends **2007-12-31 → 2025-12-31**, stamped with the **10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Stamp | as-of 2026-06-30 (last complete calendar month; no partial months in a stamped run) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 42 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Signal (level) | `btd_assets` = (Pretax − IncomeTaxExpense / statutory-rate) / Assets; **ranking signal `btd_neg = −btd_assets`** so top tercile = LOWEST gap (long "clean"), bottom = HIGHEST gap (short "aggressive") |
| Statutory rate | **35 %** for fiscal years ending < 2018, **21 %** from 2018 (TCJA); the 2018 off-calendar blended-rate nuance is ignored (documented simplification) |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short, rank fresh signals into **terciles**, long top / short bottom, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** These are large-cap survivors, where book-tax differences are
*smallest and best-behaved* — Hanlon's effect bites hardest in the broad cross-section (small,
distressed, tax-shelter-heavy names, none of which are here). Any red-flag effect this basket
shows is a **conservative lower bound on the noise, an upper bound on the signal**. The monthly
cross-section runs from **6 names (2010)** to **37**, averaging ≈30 through the deep middle of the
sample. No survivorship correction: named on the Signal axis. For context, **71 %** of firm-years
carry a *positive* book-tax gap (median +2.1 % of assets) — book income routinely exceeds the
tax-implied figure, so "large positive BTD" is a matter of degree, not sign.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does a large book-tax gap predict lower returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `btd_neg` (**long low-BTD, short high-BTD** — the Hanlon
direction, so a **positive** number supports the claim), one execution lag, 2010-03 → 2026-06
(**196 months**, avg cross-section 29.9 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **+20.1 bps/month** (+2.42%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | +0.75 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **+0.74** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | 0.19 |
| monthly hit rate | 49% |
| long leg / short leg | +151.9 / +131.8 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×1.29 over 196 months |

The point estimate is **right-signed** (low-BTD names beat high-BTD names, as Hanlon would have
it) but **economically small and statistically nowhere** (NW *t* = +0.74, one-sample +0.75). The
change signal `−ΔBTD/Assets` (worsening gaps → sell) is the strongest specification and still
falls short: **+37.9 bps/month, NW *t* = +1.79** — right-signed, never clears 2.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by signal)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `btd_neg`; top-minus-bottom forward drift (top = low BTD),
entered one day after the filing:

| horizon | n | top (low-BTD) | bottom (high-BTD) | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 569 | +2.80% | +3.00% | **−0.20%** | −0.15 | 47% | 0.57 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 551 | +4.95% | +7.42% | **−2.47%** | −1.43 | 49% | 0.94 |
| 252 d (≈1 y) | 541 | +15.73% | +17.35% | **−1.62%** | −0.55 | 49% | 0.73 |

**The event study leans the *other* way.** Pooled, the low-BTD names slightly *under*-perform the
high-BTD names at every horizon (long-short −0.2% to −2.5%), the terciles are near-monotone in the
**anti-Hanlon** direction (252 d, high-BTD → low-BTD: +17.35% / +16.22% / +15.73%), and no
horizon is significant (|*t*| ≤ 1.43, placebo *p* well above 0.5). So the calendar long-short
(mildly pro-Hanlon) and the pooled drift (mildly anti-Hanlon) **disagree on the sign and agree on
the insignificance**: there is no forward-return sort in this signal on this tape, in either
direction.

## Era split — no regime rescues it

Calendar long-short, split at 2018-01-01 (the TCJA statutory-rate cut, 35 % → 21 %):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-2018 | 94 | +29.2 bps | +0.94 |
| 2018-2026 | 102 | +11.8 bps | +0.27 |

Both eras carry the same small, right-signed, insignificant positive; neither clears the bar, and
the effect is weaker (not stronger) after the rate cut. Not a live edge that decayed — it never
certified.

## The mechanism doesn't replicate either — earnings persistence is flat across BTD

Hanlon's *actual* headline result is about **earnings persistence**, not returns: firms with large
book-tax differences have earnings that persist less. We test it directly — an interaction OLS of
next-year pretax ROA on this-year ROA, letting the persistence slope differ between the highest-
and lowest-BTD terciles (n = 530 matched firm-years):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| pooled persistence slope *b* | **+0.750** |
| low-BTD tercile persistence | **+0.750** |
| high-BTD tercile persistence | **+0.752** |
| interaction (high − low) *d* | **+0.002** |
| *t* on the interaction | **+0.03** |
| R² | 0.570 |

**Dead flat.** On this large-cap survivor panel, high-book-tax-gap firms' earnings persist
*exactly as much* as low-gap firms' (+0.752 vs +0.750, interaction *t* = +0.03). Unlike a signal
whose accounting mechanism is bulletproof even when the return edge is priced away, **here even
the mechanism is absent** — the red flag simply does not mark less-persistent earnings among these
names. (The pooled *t* ignores firm/year clustering; the point is the near-zero *magnitude*, not
the *t*.) This is consistent with Hanlon's own caveat that the effect concentrates in the broad
cross-section, not among the largest, cleanest, most-scrutinised filers.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + signal panel with a TUNABLE planted Hanlon effect (low-BTD names drift up);
no network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **+0.31** (sd 0.67), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **0/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.35 (seed 856) | **+2.55** (mean +62.8 bps/month) |

The detector sits at ≈0 on the null (zero crossings of |t| = 2 in twelve HAC *t*'s) and lights up
on a planted effect. The real-tape NW *t* = +0.74 is therefore a genuine near-null, not a broken
pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.05 — a slow annual balance-sheet signal):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | +15.0 bps/mo | +1.80%/yr | +0.55 | 0.14 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | +9.8 bps/mo | +1.18%/yr | +0.36 | 0.09 |

Costs are small (low turnover), but that is moot: the edge is **statistically indistinguishable
from zero before any costs are charged** (gross NW *t* = +0.74). You cannot get paid for a spread
you cannot certify.

## Verdict

- **Signal (returns) — WEAK.** The forward-return long-short is **right-signed** (low-BTD beats
  high-BTD, +2.4%/yr gross) and the change variant reaches **NW *t* = +1.79**, so there is a faint
  echo of the Hanlon direction — but the primary **never clears *t* = 2** (NW +0.74, one-sample
  +0.75), the pooled event drift is if anything **mildly anti-Hanlon** (−0.2% to −2.5%, all
  insignificant, placebo *p* > 0.5) and **non-monotone the wrong way**, and neither era certifies.
  A genuinely **mixed, uncertified** result — the desk's `WEAK`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Not certifiable even gross (NW *t* < 1); net of realistic long-short
  costs + borrow it is +0.36 to +0.55 *t*, Sharpe ≈ 0.1. No paycheck.
- **"Do large book-tax differences mark less-persistent earnings?" — NOT DETECTED.** The
  mechanism that anchors the claim is **flat** on this basket: high-BTD earnings persist exactly as
  much as low-BTD earnings (interaction +0.002, *t* = +0.03). On large, clean, heavily-covered
  filers, neither the return prediction nor its earnings-persistence engine shows up. The famous
  accounting red flag, applied to blue chips, is a non-event.
